claims.text: Augment reports that between November 2025 and July 2026, size-adjusted output per active developer across Augment engineering rose from 12.3 to 55.7, a 4.5x increase.
Augment reports that raw pull requests per active developer rose from 16.6 to 45.5 (2.7x) between November 2025 and July 2026.
Augment reports that lines changed per active developer rose from 8,031 to 35,147 (4.4x) between November 2025 and July 2026.
Augment built its internal software factory on Augment Cosmos, its platform for running and coordinating agents, and added each component as a new bottleneck appeared.
In Augment's software factory, specialized agents automate the mechanical work at each SDLC transition while humans retain ownership of consequential decisions.
Factory announced on September 15, 2026 that it raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing its total funding to over $400 million.
Factory's investors in the round include Blackstone, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, Evantic Capital, Sound Ventures, NEA, Mantis VC, and Clearlake.
Factory says its platform can be deployed in the cloud, on-premises, or in fully air-gapped environments, and lets enterprises control how the software factory learns and which models it uses.
GitLab 19.4, released September 17, 2026, put /goal in GitLab Duo CLI into public beta, turning an open-ended objective into a governed agentic flow.
GitLab 19.4 lets flows run when a merge request opens and exposes GitLab to any MCP client through a governed set of tools.
GitLab Credits usage visibility became generally available in GitLab 19.4 so platform owners can measure and control the costs of agentic automation.
On October 6, 2026 GitLab announced the foundation for a 'governed software factory', aimed at replacing fragmented shadow software factories.
GitLab's GitLab Security Standard defines five controls to reduce the time from detection to verified remediation in agentic software development.
GitLab's announcement brings containers and packages into one control plane alongside source code management and CI pipelines.
On October 7, 2026 OutSystems announced general availability of Agent Experience, opening its platform and Enterprise Context Graph to coding agents including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Kiro.
In GitLab 19.5, after a one-time `glab govern setup`, externally connected agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex can be connected to GitLab AI Governance via the glab CLI.
GitLab 19.5 AI Governance captures each qualifying agent session, including who ran it, which agent, which project, and when.
VMware Tanzu Platform 11.0, dated October 23, 2026, introduces an agentic performance dashboard, an agentic trace detail view, and structured logging.
OpenAI built Pando, a new Git backend, without interrupting engineering work or changing how its team uses Git.

Pando targets horizontally scalable writes optimized for concurrent pushes to many branches, with a coordinator instructing nodes to perform the update once a majority acknowledges a pre-commit message.
GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) v1.2.0, released November 4, added artifact-backed durable workflow continuation so work can carry across agents.
gh-aw v1.2.1, released November 6, made security reviews fail closed when unresolved and added a warning for dynamic checkout refs.
OpenAI's November 9, 2026 case study says CodeRabbit uses Codex to ship 20 times more software with the same engineering team.
ClickHouse announced on November 9, 2026 that it acquired Xata, an agent-native Postgres company, to give developers and agents isolated, production-like data environments on demand.

Thrum, announced November 10, 2026, is a multi-agent coordination platform for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor supporting coordinator-reviewer workflows with approval loops, with a free tier and a Pro plan at $15/month or $120/year.
